scope: Read-only source review; no reviewer-run execution, TSan or GPU claim. Executable findings are attributed to retained backend-agent evidence.

findings.assessment: blk_leaf retains the element before emitter blk_free drops its shared array handle; count-one redirect still preserves returned child.

Each copied shared ARR element acquires an ownership reference before parent handle decrement; unshared inputs move children then shallow-free. Same-array pair handles balance through retained children and two handle drops.
term_peek uses existing atomic-half rfc_view; final reference release acquires before destroying target. Existing format retained.

CAS loop uses low U32 slot, wraps index via blk_at, returns previous value, rounds fadd through F32. Ordinary concurrent whole-word reads against atomic low-word writes are not established race-safe by this review.

Initial ownership review found no blocking ownership defect but did not detect inherited alias-order defect. Backend executable counterexample reports expected119 versus candidate02 199; current source correction returns original array first and fresh copy second, matching upstream/JS alias behavior. Correction execution is pending final candidate validation.

limitations: Source reasoning is not a memory/thread-safety proof.
Unsafe concurrent structural reads or writes outside atomics are not covered.
